claims.statement: The standard of proof for every crate under crates/ is agreement with the upstream reference implementation rather than self-consistency, and the suites are split accordingly: roundtrip.rs / apply.rs / decode.rs / convert.rs exercise the crate alone, interop.rs runs the upstream binary as a child process, and where a reference cannot be run a pinned reference-made artifact or a generated vector file stands in for it.

Interop tests skip rather than fail when their reference binary is absent: each suite probes first and returns early after printing a note to stderr, so a green cargo test only proves no regression on what the machine could exercise. chd-rs resolves chdman (and ffmpeg in ld.rs) through $CHDMAN/$FFMPEG and then $PATH; xso-rs resolves maxcso through $MAXCSO then $PATH via common::maxcso_binary(); xdelta-rs probes with `xdelta3 -V`; xps-rs probes with `flips --version`.

CI's dependency step runs `apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=3 update` and installs mame-tools (whose chdman), xdelta3 and ffmpeg - all three commented as being only for the crates' tests, which skip without them - so the chd-rs parity suites and the xdelta-rs comparison execute on every run, while neither maxcso nor flips is installed and the xso-rs and xps-rs interop tests always skip in CI and are a local responsibility.

xso-rs/tests/interop.rs proves mutual readability in both directions for CSO and ZSO at 2 KiB and 64 KiB blocks: xso_rs output is decompressed by maxcso back to the original image, and maxcso --format=cso1/--format=zso output is decompressed by xso_rs back to the original image.

same_bytes_as_maxcso_zlib_cso asserts our CSO is byte-identical to `maxcso --format=cso1 --only-zlib` at block sizes 2048 and 16384, and deliberately uses the pseudo-text write_text_iso fixture (256-word vocabulary with a squared frequency skew) because ties between equal-sized zlib trials make trial order observable; ZSO has no such test since maxcso cannot run LZ4 HC 16 itself.

gdi-rs establishes agreement without running gdidrop: tests/convert.rs pins the exact descriptor gdidrop wrote at port time (including the jump to sector 45000 caused by REM HIGH-DENSITY AREA and the skipped pregaps), requires a near-miss comment 'REM HIGH-DENSITY AREA (TOC)' not to trigger that jump, and requires a single-BIN set to produce the same layout and track bytes as its split equivalent.

nsz-rs's crypto acceptance gate is cross-language and generated: scripts/gen_vectors.py drives the actual Python nsz primitives (nsz.nut.aes128, nsz.nut.Keys) from $NSZ_SRC with Keys.crc32_checksum disabled, and emits the DO-NOT-EDIT file tests/common/vectors_gen.rs holding titlekek, key-area-key, title-key-unwrap, seekable-CTR (offsets 0..1048591), XTSN (sectors 0,1,2,255,256) and mul_alpha_le vectors that tests/vectors.rs asserts in both directions.

Because synthetic keys can never satisfy the CRC32 source checks, the suites build their Keys with Keys::from_str(text, false) from the generated sources plus a fixed header_key; key-length validation still applies, so a 15-byte titlekek_source is an error.

Fixtures are generated deterministically rather than shipped: seeded xorshift writers produce ISO, CD-frame, hard-disk-image, ROM-like and CUE/GDI data into a tempfile TempDir so a failure is reproducible from its seed, and the shapes are chosen for the codec (all-zero, high-redundancy, incompressible and counting sectors; every gdi sector distinct so a mis-dropped pregap shows; chd fixtures with noise runs so not every hunk compresses). Committed media fixtures exist only where a reference tool produced them - crates/xdelta-rs/tests/data and crates/xps-rs/tests/data - located through env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), and the shared helpers live in tests/common/mod.rs (xso-rs, gdi-rs, nsz-rs) with #![allow(dead_code)].

tests/common/mod.rs in nsz-rs constructs properly encrypted NCAs from scratch - header encrypted with XTSN under a fixed header_key, wrapped title keys in the four keyblock slots, CTR sections using the real per-section counter, a common ticket with the title key under titlekek 0, and a Meta NCA whose PFS0 holds a CNMT listing each content NCA's SHA-256 - which lets pipeline.rs assert exact decrypted plaintext, which sections were decrypted, and CNMT verification counts without shipping retail content.

Malformed input must error rather than panic: xdelta-rs/tests/decode.rs tries every truncation and a byte flipped at every position of a patch (only a panic or hang fails, since some flips land where nothing checks), xps-rs/tests/apply.rs does the same sampled at (len/500).max(1), and nsz-rs/tests/malformed.rs targets allocations sized by untrusted header fields (NCZSECTN 1<<40, i64::MAX, -1; NCZBLOCK with i32::MAX blocks; PFS0 with u32::MAX counts or a u64::MAX member offset).

The nsz-rs malformed suite also pins deliberate tolerance rather than rejection: a PFS0 whose string table is one byte with no terminator must still decompress, NCAs with no CNMT fail under strict verification but are reported unverified without it, and a container with no NCAs succeeds even under strict.

The progress contract is asserted per crate: xps_rs::apply and xdelta_rs::decode callbacks must sum to the patch size, xso_rs::compress to the ISO and xso_rs::decompress to the packed file, gdi_rs::convert to the BIN total matching gdi_rs::input_size including dropped pregaps, chd_rs::create_cd to chd_rs::cd_input_size and to the fixture's exact frame bytes while chd_rs::extract_cd and extract_ld sum to the CHD's logical_size, and nsz-rs adds progress_follows_compression_not_read_ahead, which runs a BKTR update NSP on a one-thread pool and requires every callback to stay under a quarter of the total so the BKTR read-ahead cannot make the bar jump.

Every crate tests the .part contract in the form its format allows: xso-rs and nsz-rs truncate a packed file so the decode fails mid-write and assert the pre-existing output still reads 'keep me', that no <output>.part survives, and that a later complete run does replace it; xdelta-rs and xps-rs use a one-bit-flipped source (WrongSource) and prove nothing was left behind by counting directory entries; gdi-rs blocks a track's .part with a directory to show a half-written set is neither committed nor over-cleaned; chd-rs shows a CUE naming a missing BIN errors with that name in the message leaving neither disc.chd nor disc.chd.part.

nsz-rs/tests/pipeline.rs pins lazy key loading with a loader that panics if called: an NCA-free container compresses and decompresses with no keys at all, while an NCA-bearing one fails the run naming prod.keys and leaves the previously written NSZ byte-identical with no .part behind.

Two tests in the crates are ignored: xso-rs/tests/interop.rs's index_shift_round_trips builds a sparse ~2 GiB image, asserts probe reports index_shift 1, round-trips it through xso_rs (and maxcso when available), works in tempdir_in(env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")) and compares a MiB at a time; chd-rs/tests/ld.rs's large_laserdiscs_match_chdman handles a >2 GiB OpenDML capture that extracts to a RIFF AVIX split (some 7 GiB of disk), also in CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, deleting the source AVI before extracting.

The documented way to run the ignored slow tests is `cargo test --release -p <crate> -- --ignored` (for xso-rs the 2 GiB case, about 35 s; for chd-rs the >2 GiB LaserDisc), while a plain `cargo test -p <crate>` skips both ignored tests and tests whose reference tool is missing.

The crates are executed as part of the workspace: `cargo test --workspace --features oxyromon/server` locally (test.sh is the same command under cargo llvm-cov), and in CI that llvm-cov step is what actually runs them since clippy only lints test targets. The root package adds the cross-crate check tests/crates.rs, which requires the seven copied src/bin/<cli>/ui.rs files (chdrs, ciars, gdirs, nszrs, wuxrs, xdeltars, xpsrs) to be byte-identical to xso-rs's.

Interop coverage is narrowed where the reference tool is buggy or where the crate diverges on purpose: xps-rs only asks Flips for --ips and --bps-delta because Flips 2.01 crashes creating linear BPS and shrinking IPS (those cases are hand-built in apply.rs), and the xdelta-rs loop over seven xdelta3 configurations accepts Error::Unsupported mentioning DJW for -S djw while panicking on any other failure.

chd-rs's entire integration suite drives the chdrs CLI and is gated by #![cfg(feature = "cli")] in all four files, so with the cli feature off - how oxyromon depends on the crate - the tests compile to nothing; the binary itself is declared required-features = ["cli"].

chd-rs's parity rule splits codecs by what decides the bytes: `none` CHDs are compared to chdman's byte for byte, while the codecs whose bytes depend on the linked library - deflate (flate2's zlib-rs, a zlib-ng port) and Zstandard (the zstd crate's bundled 1.5.7) - and those chd-rs encodes with a different encoder - LZMA (lzma-rust2) and FLAC (rusty_flac) - are compared by the header's raw and data SHA-1s at bytes 64..104 with chdman additionally verifying our CHD; CHDRS_STRICT_PARITY=1 tightens only the deflate/zstd cases to byte-for-byte, never LZMA or FLAC.

cd.rs covers eleven CD parser paths (shared and split BINs with pregaps/postgap, RW/RW_RAW subcode, a WAV track, a disc longer than chdman's work buffer ending mid-hunk, a bare ISO, a GD-ROM GDI, the Redump two-density CUE, and both multisession shapes) for both createcd and extractcd; extraction must reproduce chdman's CUE/GDI/TOC and every BIN byte for byte while progress sums to the CHD's logical size.

write.rs proves write-path interchangeability for hard disks, DVDs and parent-relative clones - chdman reads what chdrs wrote (verify plus extracthd back to the original image, with -ip for clones) and chdrs reads what chdman wrote - and pins chdman's never-cleared 256-hunk work buffer, whose stale bytes land in a partly filled last hunk (or the parent's, when cloning).

ld.rs generates LaserDisc AVIs with ffmpeg across every layout chdman reads (interlaced NTSC, PAL, 60 fps progressive mono, 8-bit audio, UYVY, left-predicted HuffYUV, plus raw YUV frames carrying hand-built 24-bit Manchester VBI codes on lines 16-18 whose picture numbers sometimes disagree); because their audio is FLAC-coded by rusty_flac, it requires chdman to verify chdrs's CHDs and their header hashes to equal chdman createld's rather than the same bytes, while chd_rs::extract_ld's AVI must still equal chdman extractld's byte for byte.

cli.rs pins chdrs's reports as well as its bytes: a golden ISO_INFO string fixes `chdrs info` for the repository DVD fixture unconditionally even with no chdman installed, info/verify must agree with chdman over three fixtures after chdman's banner and carriage-return progress are stripped, and the (RDSK) LaserDisc fixture is excluded because avhu is not ported.

On a corrupt header chdrs diverges from the reference on purpose and the suite pins it: flipping the first byte of the header's raw SHA-1 makes `chdrs verify` exit non-zero and print the header value then the computed value to stderr, where chdman exits successfully.

cia-rs is checked against ctrtool two ways: tests/kat.rs hashes the committed fixture CIA's extracted parts against the DAT entry it was built with, and tests/interop.rs compares every part `ctrtool -p` extracts byte for byte with unpack, skipping unless ctrtool is found through $CTRTOOL or $PATH.

cia-rs/tests/edge_cases.rs builds synthetic CIAs that each break one thing — header size, type, format version, truncated sections, TMD signature type, version or group hashes, a content past the container, the highest content index — and requires a clean Error rather than a panic.

wux-rs's tests run against a synthetic Wii U disc that tests/common/mod.rs builds and encrypts with made-up disc, common, title and vWii keys, plus an update as a NUS folder; tests/wua.rs reads the WUAs back with the independent zarust ZArchive reader and pins refusals for missing keys, a damaged hashed block, a non-disc file and a duplicated title.

tests/revert.rs checks that a WUA of the disc and its update reverts to NUS folders byte for byte and that a WUA without revert data refuses to revert, and tests/nus.rs checks a disc's conversion to an installable folder and that a damaged content fails its TMD hash.

crates/wux-rs/tests/real.rs holds five #[ignore]d tests that skip unless WUXRS_DISC names a real WUD or WUX, taking keys from WUXRS_KEYS or Cemu's keys.txt, comparing with a Cemu-made WUA in WUXRS_WUA and an update in WUXRS_ADD when set, and rebuilding the disc from its WUA.

tests/disc.rs rebuilds the synthetic disc from its WUA byte for byte as a WUD and a WUX, and checks that two discs sharing an update under different disc keys share one decrypted store entry, that without a store the update stays in the WUA, that a missing or damaged entry fails the rebuild, that off-layout sectors are kept whole, and that a vWii title needs the vWii common key to be decrypted.

tests/nus.rs and tests/revert.rs check that converting into an earlier output replaces it, while a folder in the way holding anything else, a user's file or another title's NUS folder, is refused and left as it was, with no .part folder behind.
wux-rs's keys unit tests extract both common keys from a dummy otp.bin and assert that a short binary file and a 1 KiB file with no programmed common key slot are both refused with Unsupported.
